obtained.how: the publisher's typeset PDF posted on the first author's lab website (Vander Zanden lab, Center for Limnology, University of Wisconsin–Madison), 10 pages

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the first page (PDF p. 1)
bibliography.note: authors (M. Jake Vander Zanden, Yvonne Vadeboncoeur, Sudeep Chandra), year, title, Ecosystems 14: 894–903 (issue 6 per Crossref), doi:10.1007/s10021-011-9454-6 all match. printed page = PDF page + 893

claims.claim: across 546 fish populations in 75 lakes, reliance on littoral carbon averaged 57 % (lake means, each species weighted equally)
claims.location: p. 894 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 897 (PDF p. 4), Results
claims.quote: fish species not weighted according to production or biomass) averaged 57%
claims.conditions: δ13C two-end-member mixing model (littoral–benthic against pelagic + terrestrial end-members, from the most 13C-enriched littoral primary consumers and pelagic consumers), no trophic fractionation; per-species values outside 0–1 (< 10 %) set to 0 or 1; lakes with end-members < 5 ‰ apart excluded; 75 lakes of 0.02 to > 82,000 km² on five continents. Lake means (BRL) 0.57 ± 0.20 SD; the mean over all 546 populations was 0.50 ± 0.28
claims.note: the source stresses that it "cannot be extrapolated to whole-lake fish production" (abstract, p. 894): it is an average over species, not over fish biomass. BRL did not vary with mean depth, area, TP, Secchi, chlorophyll or latitude

tried.note: repository record without a full-text file

notes: Only §3.7.9 cites this paper. show.mjs also lists §3.2.5, §3.8.7 and src/w3/littoral3.js:39 under this key, but those cite Vander Zanden & Gratton 2011 (CJFAS), a different paper (see its evidence file); the ledger's matching should be fixed. Other values: benthic algae made up 36 % of whole-lake primary production on average (BPf 0.36 ± 0.24, range 0.01–0.87; the model's benthic maximum rate fixed at 30 mg C m⁻² h⁻¹, macrophytes left out, so a minimum estimate), and BPf fell with mean depth (BPf = −0.21·log(mean depth) + 0.57), so shallow lakes like Hot Brook's sit at the high end; littoral reliance exceeded BPf in 60 of 75 lakes.
